replies.text: @RepStutzman This bill is going to leave 16 million people without health insurance.

The Big Beautiful Bill’s Medicaid reforms are a start, but let’s be real—5.1% improper payments (mostly paperwork errors) don’t justify slashing $880B while ignoring the real grift. The bill’s $1.6T in cuts barely scratches the $6T needed to fix D.C.’s spending addiction.

Medicaid’s meant to protect vulnerable Americans, yet Section 3 of H.R.1 still lets Big Pharma overcharge by billions through rigged contracts and patent abuse. Redirect that waste to actual care—not bureaucratic reshuffling.

Audit every dollar, yes, but don’t pretend trimming administrative fat solves systemic rot. Real strength means crushing the $200B in annual Medicare fraud first, not squeezing patients.
